title: Jaishankar Tells Rubio Understanding Cricket Is Test of India's Friendship
excerpt: The light-hearted Mumbai exchange, citing Saurabh Netravalkar, came alongside Rubio's 26/11 tribute and talks on trade, energy and defence
body:
• External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar told U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Mumbai: “You won’t be counted as a friend of India until you really understand cricket,” noting U.S. cricketer Saurabh Netravalkar hails from Mumbai.
  • Rubio laid a wreath at the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel memorial honouring victims of the November 26, 2008 attacks, including six American citizens.
  • The Mumbai talks covered trade, energy, technology, defence and people-to-people ties, with Rubio travelling on to Jamnagar on October 21 for energy talks.
  • For diaspora readers, the cricket exchange and the Netravalkar reference underline a people-to-people link that sits alongside the trade and energy negotiations.

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar gave U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio a light-hearted test of friendship during Rubio’s Mumbai visit on Tuesday. “You won’t be counted as a friend of India until you really understand cricket,” Jaishankar said, according to Inshorts, which reported the exchange from his remarks on X. He noted that U.S. cricketer Saurabh Netravalkar hails from Mumbai.

"You won’t be counted as a friend of India until you really understand cricket."

— S. Jaishankar, External Affairs Minister of India

The remark was a brief cultural aside in a packed diplomatic day. Rubio is in India for a three-day visit from October 20 to 22 to advance ties in energy, trade and investment, defence and critical technologies, according to PTI reporting in The Hindu BusinessLine. It is his second India visit this year, after a May trip when he held talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Jaishankar and attended a Quad foreign ministers’ meeting.

A solemn start at the Taj memorial

Rubio’s Mumbai programme included a wreath-laying at the Taj memorial to honour victims of the 26/11 terror attacks. The Hindu BusinessLine, citing the Ministry of External Affairs schedule, reported he was due to land at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport at 2.15 p.m. and attend the wreath-laying at the Taj. IANS reported the same schedule, with the wreath-laying at 3.40 p.m., talks with Jaishankar at 3.50 p.m. and a “Freedom 250” reception at 6.35 p.m. to mark the 250th anniversary of U.S. independence.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=c8qmFRFNr1I

In a post quoted in live coverage of the visit, Rubio wrote: “At the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, I laid a wreath honoring the victims of the horrific November 26, 2008 terrorist attacks, including six American citizens. We remember those lost, honor the courage of those who responded, and reaffirm the enduring U.S.-India partnership and our shared commitment to combating terrorism.” IANS noted 166 people were killed in the attacks, including six Americans. The Hindu BusinessLine put the toll at over 160 people, including six U.S. nationals.

What the two ministers discussed

Jaishankar said after the meeting that the two shared views on further advancement of ties, focusing on trade, energy, technology, defence and people-to-people ties, and exchanged views on regional developments. Rubio said they discussed energy security and defence cooperation while reaffirming the importance of advancing the U.S.-India strategic partnership. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri and U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor were present, according to coverage of the meeting.

Earlier the same day, Jaishankar, Rubio and UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan held a trilateral meeting in Mumbai on regional energy security and shared economic priorities, Rubio said in a separate post.

At the Freedom 250 reception, Rubio said he believed the U.S.-India relationship is defining what the 21st century can look like, and that the two countries are aligned on using superintelligence for the betterment of humanity while mitigating its harms. That reception appearance is separate from the bilateral talks and should not be confused with a trade announcement. No signed trade agreement was announced in the reports read for this article.

Why the cricket line landed

Netravalkar’s name did specific work in Jaishankar’s remark. A Mumbai-born cricketer now representing the United States is, in one reference, an example of the people-to-people ties both ministers listed among the talks’ themes. For Indian-American readers who follow both Indian and U.S. cricket, the line connects a formal strategic partnership to a familiar, lived link between the two countries. It does not change policy, and the reports do not present it as a policy proposal. It was a light-hearted exchange, reported as such.

What’s next

Rubio travels to Jamnagar in Gujarat on Wednesday, October 21, according to both IANS and The Hindu BusinessLine. The Jamnagar stop, home to Reliance’s refining hub, keeps energy at the centre of the trip. Readers tracking the visit should watch for any concrete statements after Jamnagar, rather than treating the Mumbai cricket exchange or the Freedom 250 remarks as outcomes on trade or energy.
